name: Other oral products (case-by-case)
anchor: sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant schedules with the Germany BVL 2017 TOOTHPASTE tier as the oral-mucosal anchor for formulated products, and Canada SOR/2018-83's mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling as the article anchor
native_basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
native_basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of product as sold (ug/kg). Not a dietary maximum level and not a migration/leachate value.
scope_note: Residual routing destination for oral-cavity products that do not fit rows 1-9, dispositioned case-by-case at the Step 0 category lock. Until that lock clears, the row publishes the strictest oral-cavity anchor available in this category — the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier — as the default floor for a FORMULATED product, taken as a disclosed read-across on every anchored cell because the exact form is by definition not yet determined. If the product routed here is an ARTICLE rather than a formulated product (a mouthguard, an appliance case, an intraoral device accessory), this row's values do NOT apply: the article contract used by the toothbrushes, floss, irrigator and tongue-scraper rows applies instead, and the row is re-derived at the Step 0 lock. Nothing certifies on this row without that lock.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(colourant|colorant|colour additive|color additive|migration|leachate|food-contact|accessible part|candy as sold|as consumed|wet weight|toy))(?=.*(cosmetic|finished toothpaste|finished oral))
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor on a formulated oral row must be a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished oral-product) total-content instrument, and the guard's positive test admits only a basis that says so: 'cosmetic', 'finished toothpaste' or 'finished oral'. It rejects three families that would otherwise conflate bases: colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications (21 CFR 73/74, the India permitted-colours entry), which cap one raw material and not the finished product; migration and leachate values (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy migration, food-contact migration), which measure release rather than content; and DIETARY maximum levels, which are now excluded structurally rather than by keyword, because a food-commodity maximum level cannot satisfy a positive test for a cosmetic basis. This guard was corrected on 2026-08-17. Its earlier form also admitted any register row whose basis read 'product as sold'. Measured against the register on 2026-08-17, that admitted 176 rows to a guard whose published purpose was to exclude dietary values, 99 of them carrying no cosmetic basis at all: 84 Singapore Food Regulations maximum levels, the Mexican NOM-186 cocoa-butter lead value (100 ug/kg, STRICTER than this row's published lead value and therefore capable of binding it), the GSO concentrated-juice value and the Japanese pet-food values. No shipped number was ever in the wrong basis, because no dietary id was named and the audit scope would not surface one, but the sole mechanical firewall against the conflation Method v2.0 forbids was inoperative and its published description was refutable from the register the document cites as its own source. The property verified after the correction is stated as an invariant rather than as a row count, because the register is appended to continuously and any fixed count would go stale: EVERY row that passes this guard carries 'cosmetic' in its basis, and NO row whose product scope is a food, feed or fertiliser commodity passes. Both halves are re-checkable against the register at any time by applying this guard string to each row's basis and basis_class, which is exactly how the compiler applies it. A basis failure resolves the cell to a GAP and fails the build rather than publishing a number in the wrong basis.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), Category 20 Oral Care: a formulated oral product takes the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant maximum in its as-sold basis, with the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier read across to non-toothpaste oral-mucosal forms where it is stricter; an oral-care article takes the Canadian mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling and is otherwise held under component-level control. Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total lead content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier
Pb.label: The exact cell is unregulated: no sovereign publishes a lead value for this product form. Germany BVL 2017's toothpaste tier (0.5 mg/kg) is the nearest applicable sovereign cell because it is the only sovereign lead value written for a product applied to the oral mucosa and partly swallowed, which is this form's exposure pattern. The directly applicable German general-cosmetic tier is 2 mg/kg; HMTc reads the stricter oral tier across rather than taking the looser general value, and discloses that choice here rather than presenting the number as direct regulatory alignment.
Pb.substantiation: This is the Category 15 precedent applied to its home matrix: the BVL toothpaste tier was read across to mucosal-contact products in the live Feminine Care standard on the reasoning that oral mucosa is the closest regulated analogue to other mucosa. Here the analogy is tighter still, because the target form is itself an oral-cavity product. The read-across moves the value DOWN from the directly applicable general-cosmetic tier (2000 to 500 ug/kg), so it cannot be characterised as a convenience selection.

Cd.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total cadmium content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier
Cd.label: The exact cell cannot be identified until the Step 0 lock fixes the product form, so no instrument can be said to regulate it directly. The Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier is read across as the strictest oral-cavity anchor available in this category; it is equal to the strictest general-cosmetic value for this analyte, so the read-across is not a stretch in either direction.
Cd.substantiation: Every anchored cell on this residual row is tagged read-across rather than regulatory alignment precisely because the form is undetermined. A Step 0 lock re-derives the row against the instrument family that matches the determined form before anything certifies.

iAs.rationale: iAs carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tAs (iAs <= tAs), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
iAs.reference_method: iAs speciation reflexed when the parent total reaches min(species limit, 50 percent of the parent-total limit); the species never substitutes for the parent-total report.

Ni.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total nickel content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Korean residual finished-cosmetic nickel tier
Ni.source_scope: cosmetic products other than eye makeup or color makeup products
Ni.label: No sovereign names nickel in an oral-care product. Korea MFDS is the only jurisdiction in the register that sets a finished-cosmetic nickel content limit at all, and it tiers it by product type: eye makeup 35 ug/g, colour makeup 30 ug/g, and all other cosmetic products 10 ug/g. An oral-care product is neither eye makeup nor a colour cosmetic, so the residual 'other products' tier — the STRICTEST of the three — is the nearest applicable sovereign cell and is read across. The named anchor is MFDS Notice No. 2025-63 (Cosmetics Safety Standards), the current Korean instrument. HMTc does not use the looser makeup tiers.
Ni.substantiation: Nickel is a mucosal and contact sensitiser and reaches oral-care formulations through hydrated-silica and calcium-carbonate abrasives, mineral pigments, and stainless-steel process contact, so the cell must not be left without a ceiling where a sovereign anchor exists. The exact cell (nickel in a dentifrice, rinse, whitening system or denture-care product) is unregulated in every jurisdiction surveyed, which is why the value is published as a disclosed read-across tagged 'read-across' rather than as regulatory alignment; in Korea a dentifrice is a quasi-drug rather than a cosmetic, so the Korean cosmetic tier does not reach this form by its own terms. Two Korean notices state the same three-tier allowance at identical values: Notice 2024-9 Article 6(2) (kr_mfds2024_9_ni_other_cosmetics_10ugg) and the current Notice No. 2025-63 (the named anchor). The later notice is cited so that this standard and the Category 2 children's-dentifrice standard, which anchors the same cell, cite the same current instrument rather than splitting across two Korean notices for one number. The value is 10000 ug/kg under either notice, neither register row is flagged superseded, and the 2024-9 row remains inside this row's audit scan.
